segments.narration: Someone built a stone city on a Pacific reef. Pohnpei, Micronesia. Ninety-two artificial islands, stacked like firewood.
The walls are natural basalt columns, hexagonal logs of rock, laid crosswise like a log cabin.
The total is estimated at three quarters of a million tonnes, moved without wheels, without metal, without draught animals.
Radiocarbon dates put the megalithic building around eleven eighty, under a dynasty called the Saudeleur.
Local tradition says two brothers flew the stones into place. Archaeologists think rafts and levers, and honestly nobody has proved either.
